messages:
Maria (Finance): Hey team — vendor 'AcmeCloud Ltd' (UK) just sent their March invoice. They attached a copy with a "gross-up for withholding" clause and didn't include a US W-9. They did include a UK VAT number.

Maria (Finance): Quick Qs: do we need to withhold US taxes for this supplier? Should we ask for a W-8BEN-E instead? Also wondering about VAT treatment — do we pay VAT, or is reverse charge applicable here? @Lena (Accounting) @Anil (Vendor ops) :thinking: 

Lena (Accounting): Short answer: if the supplier is a non-US entity providing services to a US company, typically we request a W-8BEN-E so they can claim foreign status and we avoid US withholding unless a treaty says otherwise.

Lena (Accounting): VAT is separate — if the supplier charged UK VAT and we're a US-headquartered buyer without a UK VAT registration, usually VAT should not be charged on exported services. But we need to confirm how AcmeCloud booked it. If they insist on VAT or gross-up, get them to explain the tax basis and provide supporting docs.

TaxBot: Quick checklist for vendor docs 📋
• Request: W-8BEN-E (for foreign entity) OR W-8ECI if they claim effectively connected income.
• Ask vendor to reissue invoice without gross-up if they can certify non-US status.
• Capture their UK VAT registration and whether VAT was charged on invoice.
• If VAT charged and we're not UK-registered, ask for VAT removal or refund documentation.
• If vendor refuses gross-up removal, escalate to Legal/Tax for treaty/gross-up calc.

Anil (Vendor ops): I'll ping AcmeCloud now and ask for a completed W-8BEN-E and a corrected invoice that removes the gross-up. I'll also request a short note from them explaining why they charged VAT (if they did). Sending now. :rocket:

Maria (Finance): Thanks — please cc me. If they push gross-up, we should get an estimate of the additional amount and hold payment pending Tax's sign-off.

Lena (Accounting): Also tagging Finance Ops playbook: when receiving W-8s, save PDF to vendor profile and set tax withholding flag accordingly in NetSuite. If they provide treaty claim, attach the certificate.

Anil (Vendor ops): Ack. I'll post reply from vendor here when they respond.

Maria (Finance): Example invoice snippet they sent:
```
Invoice #2026-034
Supplier: AcmeCloud Ltd (UK)
VAT Reg: GB123456789
Description: Monthly platform subscription - March 2026
Amount (net): 10,000.00 GBP
VAT (20%): 2,000.00 GBP
Total: 12,000.00 GBP
Note: Supplier reserves right to gross-up for any applicable withholding taxes.
```

Maria (Finance): Filing note: we don't currently have a UK VAT registration and Redwood HQ is US-based — so likely vendor shouldn't charge VAT for exported B2B services, but wait for vendor explanation. 

TaxBot: If you want, I can draft the message template to request W-8 + corrected invoice and checklist items. Type: "draft please" and I'll drop a ready-to-send message. :+1:

Maria (Finance): draft please

TaxBot: Draft below — paste to vendor and send:

```
Hi AcmeCloud,

Thanks for the invoice. To process payment we need the following documentation:
1) Completed IRS W-8BEN-E (entity) PDF signed and dated.
2) A corrected invoice removing the gross-up clause — or a written justification with legal basis if you insist on gross-up.
3) Clarification on VAT: if VAT was charged, please explain the tax treatment and provide supporting registration/memo.

Please send documents to finance@redwood.com. Payments will be held until we receive the W-8 and corrected invoice or a tax team-approved justification.

Thanks,
Finance Team (Redwood Inference)
```

Anil (Vendor ops): Sending now. Will update thread when they reply. :eyes:
